x: Over our five miles course Field finished a good winner in 30 mins. 8 secs., and Archie Bedford ran well to finish a close second with Ches Walker also well up.

The 880 yards saw Archie Bedford and Jim Kennedy running for us but up against a strong Walton trio, which included Willie Nankeville, the A.A.A. mile champion, we had to be content with 4th place through Bedford, whereas Walton scored a “ maximum ” of 8 points for this race.

In the 600 yards we had Bedford and Jim Beaumont and they had to be content with 4th and 5th positions. The 1,000 yards saw our real strength and here we had the first three home in Derrick Burfitt, Ches Walker and Vernon Blowfield, with Jimmy Wood, of the Poly, 4th.

Cope, was not competing, and Ches Walker won a good race from Archie Bedford, with Len Bishop running well for third place. Frank Kemp made a double of it by winning the 220 yards Junior race, beating Dave Marshall, who is the Surrey champion at this distance.

Archie Bedford ran well to hand over equal fourth on the first stage, especially as his opponents included E. Brown, the Mitcham lad, who won the recent South of Thames race, Bowen, of the local club, Nicholson, of Woodford Green, a most experienced runner, and Culver, of Essex Beagles, who last yea…
The course was about 8 miles and the first man home was Archie Bedford, who beat a couple of Walton boys, with Len Adams and Denis Brickwood next home for us.
Walker allowed Green to hand over with him at the end of the third stage, but Archie Bedford, Eddie Short and Bill Lucas saw to it that we maintained our unbeaten record for this race.

Archie Bedford, however, soon caught the leader and from then on we were always out in front. Len Adams kept up the good work and increased our lead and Bill Lucas took us further ahead to hand over to Mike Stearman 68 secs. to the good.

Walker just beat Eddie Short for second place, and then came Jack Braughton 5th, Bill Lucas 7th, Archie Bedford 9th and Len Herbert 11th. All the first five were selected to run for Surrey in the Inter-Counties race at York, and Jack Brown 7th in the Kent race and A.
Our "B" team of—Newell, Adams, Short and Bedford, all ran well to finish in 3rd position in front of Cambridge H., Reading A.C., and Surrey A.C., with our "C" team—Stokell, Taylor, E.
Walker put in a really fine run to put them in the lead on the 3rd stage, and this was maintained by Wright, Short, Lucas and Bedford down to the end of the 7th relay.
Len Herbert was passed by Dunckley of the Poly. on the final leg, after we had been second to T.V.H. for the first three stages, and he was followed home by Archie Bedford, who had picked up a place.

Charlie Walker again refused to cane himself over the last mile and was content with 4th. Following him were Tooby, Bedford, Burr, Trower, Brickwood, L. Bishop and Newell making one of his too infrequent appearances.

After the first half mile we had Masters, Walker and Bagnall in the first 20, with Patterson Baulch, Short, Trower and Bedford in the twenties, and although positions changed a bit, our scoring six were always placed well in the first thirty.
He came round 56 seconds in the lead at the end of the first lap and the rest of the field were fairly well strung out with Bedford making his way through from about 11th at 2 miles.

Bedford ran a good race and again was seen making his way through the field as the race progressed. Roffey and Bagnall gave of their best whilst Dave Baulch ran above form and forced himself past Ingles in the home straight to make sure we had six men home before T.V.H. had three.
Walker gained two places and Roffey put us in the lead. Bedford ran last and was caught by Knight of Essex. He immediately, perhaps unwisely, tried to drop him and we were beaten by five seconds.
Bedford and Walker then made sure of our victory though Charlie took things a little too easy in the middle and so we missed the course record by one second.

The eighth leg was run by Bedford who was only too pleased to run whereever the selectors decided and though he lost places to Norris and Clark he still gave a sterling performance and established a new club best by 10 seconds.
Approaching the end of the first lap Miller, Thompson, Glover, Bedford and Shippen were in close attendance around tenth position with John Moore moving through fast after his mishap.
Let the individual positions speak for themselves - Newell 59th, Shippen 136th, Baulch 158th, Gebbett 174th, Bedford 205th and Walker 248th.
